claims.text: Rome holds a fraction of its old people, who still think themselves heirs of empire and resent being handled; it is also the seat of the Church and of the secret Inquisition.

The rioni are held for the Clans: the Cappadocians, many named Rosselini, rule the district of the Pantheon, while districts are kept in trust for the Tzimisce and for the Ravnos should a fit claimant appear.
Camilla, a master of the Road of Sin who once studied under, and loved, Tanitbaal-Sahar, said to have founded that Road, lets Rome's Cainites do as they like and backs challenges to the Papacy.

Cretheus, Fifth Generation Ventrue and childe of Mithras, ruled Rome in fact for nearly 300 years and is the only public member of the Ignoti; bending the knee to Camilla in 1229 was read as the hidden ones' blessing.

title: Bath, the Free Fiefdom
summary: Mithras' crown in the Baronies of Avalon.

claims.text: Bath's Cainites hold that if London is the seat of Mithras, Aquae Sulis is the crown; belief in Mithras is power there, and the Unconquered Sun's Praetorians train within its bounds.
Bath was one of the few domains to refuse tribute to the Triumvirate's invasion; after Roald Snake Eyes fell, Mithras' satraps made it a free fiefdom, autonomous from the barons.
Bathing over an hour in its waters gives a vampire the toughness of one dot of Fortitude for the rest of the night.
The wooden Guildhall serves for trade and taxes by day and for trading favours by night; feeding happens only in the alleys outside.
Evnissyen's Promethean faction wants Bath rid of both pilgrims and Mithraism, and plots against the Consul Arcadius, Mithras' grandchilde.
The Salubri Bethany of Ely, once a leader of the Cainite Heresy there, fled Tremere persecution to Bath; at least five Salubri now shelter in the domain.
The Winchester Tremere covet Bath and seek to weaken the blood tie between the Unconquered and Arcadius.

title: The Mithraic Mysteries
summary: The faith of the Unconquered Sun.

claims.text: Only the worthy among Mithras' faithful earn the title Pater: leaders who wear ruby rings and jewelled robes, keep the crucible of sacrificial blood and carry prayers to Mithras.

title: Black Dogs
summary: Harbingers of death on the moors.

claims.text: Peasants of Wales and Britain tell of black dogs as large as a grown man, with ember-bright eyes, stalking travellers lost on the moors; none agree whether they are flesh or spirit.
After Olaf the Holy fell at Stiklarstadir to Thorir the Hound of Bjarkarey, the old Gangrel Viking Valborg Crooked-Eye took the island and revived the old ways in a twisted form.
The court volva Gudrunn, a Fifth Generation Cappadocian and once a famed seer of Norway, casts runes and gives doubtful prophecy.
Reavers secretly seize clergy and nobles for feast days and the midwinter blot; the Princes of the Black Cross know a bishop is held and seek mercenaries to free the captive.
Prince Alfonzo, Seventh Generation Lasombra, took the city by fear and intrigue to defy a sire in Venice, and now clings to it as a tyrant, short of allies and coin.
Malachite, the Rock of Constantinople, a Seventh Generation Nosferatu and Michael's last true believer, works to raise a new Dream; agents called the Priors watch every court, guild and monastery.
Michaelite Toreador test each arriving Toreador's blood for a soul like their Martyr's, seeking a new prophet.
Ghouls abandoned when the Trinity families burned or fled in 1204 now hunt Cainites from the Grand Bazaar.
A Frankish second son who plotted a brother's murder, Embraced by a Ventrue adviser; the most notorious of the new Cainite cult leaders who copy Michael's divinity with blood and obsession.

title: Mogadishu, the White Pearl
summary: The twin cities of Hamar and Shangani.

claims.text: The Assamites won the city after five centuries of manoeuvre, riding Islam's rise to defeat the Ramanga; the Na'ib rules and insists on public harmony among all kinds of vampires.
Distance from European Princes made it a haven for ancillae and neonates, until elders fearing Gehenna began arriving with their lineage politics and old boons.
Aphobis, Tenth Generation Setite, rules the linen trade to Egypt, hates the slave trade as an offence to Apep, and hosts malcontents at the Jade Horse inn.
Bantu, an Impundulu, and Esihle, a Bomkazi witch, are a married pair raised together from infancy.
Jakuta, a Yoruba thaumaturge of Ife who claims no lineage, woke from long torpor and has borne the names Chango, Xango and Shango.
Named for the temple of Mangaladevi, it is a heart of the spice trade; legend says the sage Parashurama reclaimed the land from the sea.
The Danava dwell in a temple there; Lasombra, Ventrue and Malkavians from Rome and Brujah from Carthage once sent childer to its shores.
The Salubri allied with the devas, while the asura half of that brood call themselves a scourge on humanity; lately the deva elders sleep and the asura neonates rise.
The Daitya, Setites who became Buddhists once they had wiped out the Children of Osiris in the Himalayas, are old allies of the Salubri; the Ravnos live in every caste.
A vassal may give a liege access to two Background dots for every Anchor Background dot the liege puts up; valued vassals may trade on reputation instead.
Coteries pool Backgrounds normally; married couples, or two men joined in enfrerement, pool holdings as one household.
Cainites favour absolute inheritance: the eldest childe in good standing, by years in the Blood and whatever the gender, inherits the sire's holdings unless the sire names another succession.
A domain's heart is its manor, the Domain Background; its points are split into aspects, and at least one dot must go to Area.
Area runs from a tower or fortified cottage for about ten people up to a walled town or district of about a thousand.
Each Security dot adds +1 difficulty to break in by stealth or force; each Prosperity dot halves the cost of Resources up to its rating and gives -1 difficulty on Commerce rolls.
Servants run from a few part-time helpers, three on a trip, to a legion of sixty in a retinue; they roll 4 dice in their main task and 2 or 3 otherwise.
After the Assize of Arms in 1181 every free English peasant household must keep a spear, gambeson and iron cap; Jews must sell any mail, and no one may stockpile beyond the law's demand.
Carrying a knife or cudgel is ordinary; the wealthy wear swords but surrender them on visits, and walking into town with several weapons signals trouble.
A pavis planted in the ground gives one crouching person Good cover.
Initiative is rolled once per fight and counted down; actions on the same number happen together, and players declare all multiple actions up front, resolved in later passes.
The first player character each turn may tag another character, who takes the tagger's initiative; delaying lets a character interrupt later actions once.
A ready longer-reach attack, like a spear or nocked arrow, goes before a shorter-reach one; a character may hustle, running and acting in one move.
Attack and defence are rolled, but separate damage and soak rolls are cut.
